title: The German student visa, explained
description: Types of student visa, the documents you need, the role of the Blocked Account and health insurance, how to apply and how long it takes.
html:
Most students from outside the EU need a visa before they can start studying in Germany. The process is well defined, but it involves several documents that have to be arranged in the right order. This guide covers the types of visa, the requirements and a realistic timeline.

Which visa

The student visa is for applicants who already hold an admission letter. The student applicant visa is for people who still need to apply or attend an entrance exam in Germany; it can be converted into a student visa after admission. Language course visas are separate and cannot be converted.

Requirements

  • Admission letter from a recognised German institution, or proof of application for the applicant visa
  • Proof of funds: for 2026, €992 for each month of the first year, which is €11,904, usually in a Blocked Account
  • Health insurance: travel cover for the visa and German cover from the start of studies
  • Passport valid beyond the planned stay
  • Proof of language proficiency in the language of your programme
  • Educational certificates, a CV and a letter of motivation
  • Biometric photos and the visa fee of €75

Health insurance

Embassies ask for two things: travel health insurance that covers you from arrival until your German cover starts, and evidence that you will have German health insurance once enrolled. Students under 30 can join the statutory system; older students and some visa types need private cover. Arranging both together, along with the Blocked Account, is the simplest way to have the file complete.

The application

Book an embassy appointment as early as possible; in some countries the wait is months. Many countries now use the online portal of the Federal Foreign Office for the application itself, with the in-person appointment reserved for biometrics and payment. Processing takes four to twelve weeks. Once in Germany, you register your address and apply for the residence permit at the immigration office within the first 90 days.

Advice from people who have done it

Start the Blocked Account as soon as you have a conditional admission; the deposit takes time to arrive from some countries. Check the embassy's document list, which can differ slightly from the general list. Bring originals and copies. And keep every confirmation email; the immigration office will ask for the same documents again.
